class_name: 話題-も観点-トシテモ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

glosses: as X as well; from X's side also
patterns.usage_note: The も version of としては: it grants that others have their positions and adds that the named party, in its own capacity, holds this one as well. Business and public speech use it constantly with institutions and with 私 to signal shared concern (市としても, 会社としましても), and it typically implies some commitment or feeling rather than a bare fact. Note that a clause plus としても is a different construction meaning "even if"; this entry is the noun-attached standpoint use.

examples.ruby: 母[はは]としても、私[わたし]の一人[ひとり]暮[ぐ]らしは心配[しんぱい]なのだろう。
examples.english: My mother, for her part, must be worried about me living alone.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]としても、練習[れんしゅう]は土曜[どよう]のほうがありがたい。
examples.english: For my part too, I'd be glad if practice were on Saturday.

examples.ruby: 学校[がっこう]としましても、給食[きゅうしょく]の見直[みなお]しを進[すす]めております。
examples.english: The school, for its part, is working on a review of the lunch program.

glosses: even (for) X; X is no exception
patterns.usage_note: Colloquial にしても, and it pushes back: you raise X, the case the listener assumed was different, and say the same thing holds for it too. That argumentative edge and the って ending keep it in speech and dialogue, where it often carries a touch of exasperation; the neutral にしても and the polite にしましても are what you write. Compare としても, which claims a standpoint of one's own instead of contesting an assumption.

examples.ruby: 先輩[せんぱい]にしたって、最初[さいしょ]は失敗[しっぱい]ばかりだったんだ。
examples.english: Even the senior guys did nothing but screw up at the start, you know.

examples.ruby: 機械[きかい]にしたって、休[やす]ませなきゃいつかは壊[こわ]れる。
examples.english: Even a machine will give out eventually if you never let it rest.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]にしたって、同[おな]じ立場[たちば]なら断[ことわ]れなかったよ。
examples.english: I couldn't have refused either, in the same position.

glosses: even if it is; granted that it is
patterns.usage_note: Built on the imperative しろ of する, which gives it a curt, assertive ring: you concede the noun in front and then press the objection that survives the concession. It is blunter than にしても, blunt enough that it lands as argument or reproof rather than gentle conversation; にせよ is its stiffer written twin. It also runs in pairs, 〜にしろ〜にしろ, to say the conclusion holds whichever alternative applies.

examples.ruby: 冗談[じょうだん]にしろ、あの言[い]い方[かた]は失礼[しつれい]すぎる。
examples.english: Joke or not, putting it that way was flat-out rude.

examples.ruby: 一時的[いちじてき]な措置[そち]にしろ、住民[じゅうみん]への説明[せつめい]は要[い]る。
examples.english: Even as a stopgap, it still has to be explained to residents.

examples.ruby: 善意[ぜんい]にしろ、勝手[かって]に決[き]められては困[こま]る。
examples.english: Well-meant or not, I can't have things decided without me.
